body:
Fixes #41096

## Problem

Ignore is linked to Normal by default, making it visible instead of
hidden. 

## Solution

Replace the default link with an explicit highlight definition:

```vim
Ignore ctermfg=0 guifg=bg
```

comment_data.body:
Hi,  I investigated the cursor test failure. 

Moving `Ignore` into the hard-coded highlight definitions changes the builtin highlight IDs because they are assigned in insertion order. That causes `lCursor`'s ID to change, which is why `cursor_spec.lua` fails.

I tried 3 approaches locally:

1. updating the expected `id_lm` value to match the new builtin ID.

2. moving Ignore to after lcursor in the hardcoded group also works.

3. According to me, the test can be made better :- 

Instead of the hardcoded highlight IDs, I replaced it with  `api.nvim_get_hl_id_by_name(...)`, so the test checks the correct highlight groups dynamically instead of depending on their numeric IDs.

All the approaches pass locally. Before I commit any test changes, I wanted to ask: what acc to you is the preferred solution.

> there is also the matter of CI

I'm reposting my reply to @echasnovski here because after I applied the suggested change, I could no longer see the original review thread.

Hi, I investigated the cursor test failure.

Moving Ignore into the hard-coded highlight definitions changes the builtin highlight IDs because they are assigned in insertion order. That causes lCursor's ID to change, which is why cursor_spec.lua fails.

I tried 3 approaches locally:

1. updating the expected id_lm value to match the new builtin ID.

2. moving Ignore to after lcursor in the hardcoded group also works.

3. According to me, the test can be made better 

Instead of the hardcoded highlight IDs, I replaced it with api.nvim_get_hl_id_by_name(...), so the test checks the correct highlight groups dynamically instead of depending on their numeric IDs.

All the approaches pass locally. Before I commit any test changes, I wanted to ask: what acc to you is the preferred solution.

> updating the expected id_lm value to match the new builtin ID.

just do that. 

> Instead of the hardcoded highlight IDs, I replaced it with api.nvim_get_hl_id_by_name(...)

it's good for tests to be robust, but some hardcoded values are useful as a signal about how changes actually flow through things. this is ~1 failing test, no need to overcomplicate it.
